metadata.name: ayni
metadata.description: Ayni — Solana implementation of AHA (Ancestral Humanity Anonymous)

instructions.name: activate_faucet
docs: The neophyte's parrain (their WingPeer) triggers the one-time gas grant —
one grant per identity commitment, ever, enforced by nullifier.

accounts.name: parrain_membership
docs: The sponsor's membership (the wing side of the WingPeer bond).

accounts.name: neophyte_membership
docs: The newcomer's membership; the grant goes to its `owner` wallet.

accounts.name: wing_peer
docs: The neophyte's designated sponsor bond — seed-bound to the neophyte, so
it can't be swapped for someone else's.

accounts.name: grant_nullifier
docs: One grant per membership commitment — `init` collision IS the refusal.
Circle-scoped: see the scope note above; cross-Circle dedup belongs to
personhood, not to a commitment that must stay unlinkable.

accounts.name: parrain
docs: The parrain (signs + pays the nullifier's rent — part of the welcome).

instructions.name: approve
docs: A Council seat approves a pending proposal.

instructions.name: approve_child_close
docs: Another foundation seat approves a pending delete-Circle vote.

instructions.name: approve_child_rotation
docs: Another foundation seat approves a pending child-rotation vote.

instructions.name: approve_federation_child
docs: F56 — a foundation Council seat vouches a child into its federation
(the consent `parent` alone cannot give).

accounts.name: circle
docs: The child to admit — must at least name this foundation as parent.

accounts.name: seat
docs: A foundation Council seat — the consent that makes federation real.

instructions.name: attest_admission
docs: Attestation A: the parrain attests for the newcomer they sponsor — one
action, one attestation per newcomer, self-attestation refused.

accounts.name: parrain_membership
docs: The parrain's own membership — in good standing, in this Circle.

accounts.name: attestation
docs: One per newcomer — `init` collision IS the refusal of a second parrain.

accounts.name: parrain
docs: A key the parrain's membership recognises (owner or guardian).

instructions.name: attest_admission_zk
docs: Attestation A, anonymous form (Epic 2): a Groth16 proof that SOME member
of the tree attests for this newcomer — the sponsor edge never exists.
Reuses the member_vote circuit + ceremony key, like prove_personhood.

accounts.name: member_tree
docs: The votable set the parrain proves membership of (current root).

accounts.name: recent_roots
docs: F54 ring buffer — pass it (after cranking `note_root`) so the proof
survives concurrent admissions; may be null for a Circle that has never
cranked, in which case only the exact current root is accepted.

accounts.name: attestation
docs: One parrain attestation per newcomer — shared PDA with the named form,
so the two forms cannot be stacked.

accounts.name: vouch_nullifier
docs: Replay guard on the vouch nullifier itself.

accounts.name: payer
docs: A relayer pays, so the parrain's wallet never appears — the same rule
as `cast_vote`.

instructions.name: begin_member_epoch
docs: F54b — begin a new member epoch: empty the tree; only live memberships
re-enter via `reinsert_member`. Any-seat housekeeping.

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (signs; pays the ring-buffer rent if first use).

instructions.name: cancel_proposal
docs: Any single Council seat cancels a pending proposal (the contest tripwire).

instructions.name: cast_vote
docs: Cast one anonymous ballot (ZK member-set inclusion + per-proposal nullifier).

accounts.name: payer
docs: A relayer pays so the voter's wallet is never linked to the ballot.

instructions.name: close_circle_profile
docs: Delist a Circle from the public directory by closing its `CircleProfile`
(the Circle itself is untouched). Any Council seat may do it; rent is
refunded to that seat.

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (receives the reclaimed rent).

instructions.name: confirm_admission
docs: Attestation B: a trusted servant (distinct person from the parrain)
co-attests — the commitment enters the votable set and the provisional
marker closes. Admission complete.

accounts.name: membership
docs: The newcomer's (provisional) membership.

accounts.name: provisional
docs: The provisional marker — closed here, one-shot: a second confirmation
has no marker left to close and fails at the constraint.

accounts.name: attestation
docs: The parrain's attestation for this newcomer, and through it the
parrain's membership — both needed for the distinct-persons rule.
Mut: `confirm_admission` pins the leaf index/epoch on it (F54).

accounts.name: parrain_membership
docs: Required for a NAMED attestation (checked in the handler against
`attestation.parrain`); pass null for an anonymous one.

accounts.name: recent_roots
docs: F54 ring buffer — pass when the Circle has one so the pre-confirmation
root stays provable and the epoch is pinned on the attestation.

accounts.name: servant
docs: Any Council seat (signs; receives the marker's rent).

instructions.name: create_member_proposal
docs: A Council seat opens a group-conscience proposal for the membership.

instructions.name: create_membership_mint
docs: Create the Circle's soulbound Token-2022 NonTransferable membership mint
(authority = Circle PDA) and register it — no external setup step (F3).

accounts.name: mint
docs: The new mint — a fresh keypair the client generates and co-signs. Created
and initialized here as a Token-2022 NonTransferable mint.

accounts.name: treasurer
docs: Must be the Council's Treasurer seat (authorizes the mint).

instructions.name: create_post
docs: A member publishes a time-boxed post (text and/or IPFS image).

accounts.name: membership
docs: The author's membership in this Circle — proves membership and ties the
post to a wallet-bound member (anonymous, owner-less memberships cannot
post; a Council seat can post via its own membership if it holds one).

instructions.name: delete_message
docs: Delete a message (sender/recipient anytime; anyone once expired).

instructions.name: delete_post
docs: Any of the 7 Council seats deletes a post (moderation by group conscience).

instructions.name: donate
docs: Donate SOL to a Circle's treasury (anyone may contribute).

instructions.name: donate_token
docs: Donate any SPL / Token-2022 token to a Circle's treasury (anyone, any
amount). For the foundation, pass the foundation Circle — see the
`fundFoundation` client helper.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: The Circle treasury PDA — the owner/authority of the treasury token
account. A plain account here (it only needs to be a valid owner pubkey).

accounts.name: treasury_token_account
docs: The treasury's token account for `mint`, owned by the treasury PDA. The
client creates it idempotently (associated token account) before/with the
donation; here we only require it belongs to the treasury for this mint.

instructions.name: end_wing_peer
docs: End a WingPeer relationship (either party). Sets active = false.

accounts.name: membership
docs: The membership the signer controls — must be the mentee or the wing.

instructions.name: establish_wing_peer
docs: A member designates (or changes) their WingPeer (mentor). Caller controls
the mentee membership; the wing must be a real member of the Circle.

accounts.name: signer
docs: A key the mentee controls (owner or guardian).

instructions.name: execute_child_close
docs: Apply a passed delete-Circle vote: close the child (and its profile).

accounts.name: child
docs: Re-assert genuine parentage at execute (defense-in-depth beyond the vote's
has_one binding): a Circle may only be closed by its real parent.

accounts.name: profile
docs: Optional: the child's directory profile, closed so it leaves the map.

instructions.name: execute_child_rotation
docs: Apply a passed child-rotation vote into the child Circle's Council.

instructions.name: execute_proposal
docs: Execute a proposal once it reaches 4-of-7 (and, for migration, once the
contest window has elapsed).

accounts.name: executor
docs: Anyone may trigger execution once the threshold is met.

instructions.name: finalize_member_proposal
docs: Close voting and record the group conscience (quorum + majority).

accounts.name: config
docs: The Circle's policy (quorum/pass thresholds). Bound to the proposal's
Circle by seeds, created on first use with safe defaults — so it can't be
swapped for a more permissive config or omitted to dodge a tighter one.

accounts.name: finalizer
docs: Anyone may finalize once the deadline has passed.

instructions.name: grant_level
docs: Grant a shamanic level along an anonymous, ZK-verified lineage.

accounts.name: nullifier_record
docs: Spent-nullifier marker. `init` fails if it already exists → replay-proof.

accounts.name: payer
docs: A relayer pays so the granting shaman's wallet never touches the chain,
preserving issuer anonymity (docs/zk-lineage.md — metadata caveat).

instructions.name: init_faucet
docs: Create the Circle's faucet jar (any Council seat; default grant amount).

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (signs + pays the jar's rent).

instructions.name: initialize_circle
docs: Create a Circle and seat its 7-seat Council (the authority) in one tx.
`parent` is the Circle this nests under (the World Service address, or a
root for the foundation); `seats` are the 7 Council members.

instructions.name: initialize_lineage
docs: Bootstrap a Circle's lineage tree with the World Service genesis credential.

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (one-time setup; signs + pays).

instructions.name: initialize_member_tree
docs: Create the Circle's member-set tree (votable population). Run once.

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (one-time setup; signs + pays).

instructions.name: install_elected_seat
docs: Install the winner of a passed seat election into the Council (F28).

instructions.name: issue_acknowledgment
docs: Issue an acknowledgment credential (course/initiation certificate),
attested by an anonymous lineage teacher. Stores only the Poseidon root
of the four blinded fields; selective disclosure happens off-chain via
`circuits/ack_disclose.circom`. Reuses the lineage verifying key.

accounts.name: membership
docs: Binds the credential to an existing member of this circle.

accounts.name: ack_nullifier
docs: Spent-nullifier marker (distinct namespace from level-grant nullifiers).

accounts.name: payer
docs: A relayer pays so the attesting teacher's wallet never touches the chain.

instructions.name: issue_membership
docs: Issue a soulbound yearly membership, identified by a ZK commitment.
`owner` is an optional controlling wallet (default() = fully anonymous);
`recovery_keys` up to two optional guardians; `require_cosign` opts into
member-co-signed migration.

accounts.name: personhood
docs: Required only when `circle.require_personhood`: a one-per-human
`PersonhoodCredential` (from `prove_personhood`), consumed here.

accounts.name: open_membership
docs: Optional admission-policy marker. Pass it (the ["openjoin", circle] PDA)
to self-admit in a permissionless Circle; omit it for Scribe-Secretary
admission. `has_one = circle` binds it to this Circle.

accounts.name: secretary
docs: Signs + pays. Must be the Scribe-Secretary seat for a gated Circle; in a
permissionless Circle (open marker present) it may be any wallet.

accounts.name: two_sponsor
docs: Epic 1 policy (["twosponsor", circle]) — required and created on first
use with `required = false`, so it can never be omitted to dodge an
enabled two-sponsor rule (the withdraw_treasury/config pattern).
Appended last so existing clients' account ordering is unchanged.

instructions.name: issue_progress_token
docs: A Council seat awards a member a progress token (milestone chip).

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (signs + pays the chip's rent).

instructions.name: issue_provisional_membership
docs: Provisional admission on the parrain's attestation: membership exists
(page live, faucet usable) but the commitment is NOT in the member tree,
so every members-only proof fails by construction.

accounts.name: policy
docs: The Circle must have opted into two-sponsor admission.

accounts.name: attestation
docs: The parrain's attestation for exactly this newcomer — the authorization.

accounts.name: provisional
docs: The provisional marker — its existence IS the status; closed on confirm.

accounts.name: personhood
docs: Required only when `circle.require_personhood` — consumed here.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Whoever pays the rent — typically the newcomer's fresh wallet (first
gas may come from the parrain or the faucet right after).

instructions.name: link_seat_election
docs: Bind a member proposal to a seat election (F28). The proposal's
description_hash must equal H("AHA-elect" || seat_index || candidate).

instructions.name: member_migrate
docs: Self-recovery: a member holding a key migrates their own membership owner
with no Council vote and no time-lock.

accounts.name: member_authority
docs: The member's current `owner` or `recovery_key`.

instructions.name: mint_membership_token
docs: Mint one soulbound membership token to a member's Token-2022 account.

accounts.name: member_token_account
docs: The member's Token-2022 account (created by the client beforehand).

accounts.name: treasurer
docs: Must be the Council's Treasurer seat (authorizes the mint).

instructions.name: note_root
docs: F54a — record the current member root into the recent-roots ring buffer
(permissionless crank; run before proving).

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone (pays the one-time PDA rent on first crank; a relayer may pay so
the prover-to-be is not named by the crank either).

instructions.name: open_maci_round
docs: Open a MACI (coercion-resistant) round over a member proposal, registering
the coordinator's encryption key. Any seat. See docs/maci.md.

instructions.name: propose
docs: A Council seat opens a proposal (RotateSeat / MigrateWallet / WithdrawTreasury).

instructions.name: propose_child_close
docs: A foundation seat opens a 4-of-7 vote to DELETE a federation Circle.

accounts.name: child
docs: The target Circle. It MUST be a direct child of `foundation`
(`child.parent == foundation`). Without this, `foundation` is a bare
caller-supplied account, so anyone could stand up a Circle they seat 4-of-7
themselves and use it as `foundation` to close ANY Circle — including the
root — stealing its rent. `parent` is immutable after `initialize_circle`,
so this binds the vote to genuine parentage for its whole life.

instructions.name: propose_child_rotation
docs: A foundation seat opens a 4-of-7 vote to rotate a child Circle's 7 seats,
valid for `validity_secs` (1–90 days).

accounts.name: child
docs: The target Circle. It MUST be a direct child of `foundation`
(`child.parent == foundation`) — enforced here, not just documented.
Without it, a caller-supplied `foundation` they seat 4-of-7 themselves
could rotate ANY Circle's Council. `parent` is immutable after creation.

instructions.name: prove_personhood
docs: Mint a one-per-human PersonhoodCredential from an anonymous proof.

accounts.name: personhood
docs: Unique per human per Circle (seeded by the personhood nullifier) — `init`
fails on a second attempt by the same human.

instructions.name: publish_maci_message
docs: Publish an encrypted MACI command (vote or key-change) to an open round.

instructions.name: publish_member_root
docs: F56 — publish an APPROVED child's member root under its foundation
(permissionless crank once approved).

accounts.name: circle
docs: The Circle being anchored — must genuinely belong to this federation.

accounts.name: federation_child
docs: The foundation's approval of this child (F56) — created only by a
foundation Council seat. Its existence at this exact PDA is the consent
gate: a rogue self-claimed child has no approval, so it cannot be
anchored. `has_one` re-binds both keys defensively.

accounts.name: recent_roots
docs: Present when the Circle has a ring buffer (carries the epoch).

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone (pays the entry's rent on first publish).

instructions.name: recover_membership
docs: Rebind a membership's owner under an executed MigrateWallet proposal
(with the member's co-signature when the membership requires it).

accounts.name: member_authority
docs: Required only when `membership.require_cosign`: the member's `owner` or
`recovery_key`. Omitted (None) for council-only recovery.

instructions.name: refill_faucet
docs: Move treasury funds into the jar under a passed anonymous member vote
whose description_hash commits to exactly (circle, amount). One-shot.

accounts.name: proposal
docs: The passed member vote committing to exactly (circle, amount).

accounts.name: fill_marker
docs: One-shot marker: a passed refill vote moves funds exactly once.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Whoever triggers the (permissionless) refill; pays the marker's rent.

instructions.name: register_messaging_key
docs: Publish the caller's x25519 messaging public key.

instructions.name: reinsert_member
docs: F54b — re-insert one live membership into the current epoch's tree
(permissionless).

accounts.name: provisional
docs: commitment; the handler only requires it to be EMPTY (never created, or
closed by `confirm_admission`) — a provisional member must not re-enter
the votable set through the rebuild side door.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone (pays the leaf-marker rent).

instructions.name: renew_membership
docs: Renew (extend) a membership for another term on donation.

accounts.name: config
docs: The Circle's policy. Created on first use (default = free renewal); its
`renew_donation_lamports` is the self-support fee. Required (not optional)
so the fee can't be bypassed by omitting it.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: The Circle treasury PDA — receives the renewal donation.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Anyone may pay to renew a membership (a member can renew anonymously,
or another member can gift a renewal).

instructions.name: revoke_membership
docs: Revoke (delete) a membership — Scribe-Secretary seat; closes the account.

instructions.name: send_message
docs: Store an end-to-end encrypted, sealed-sender message to any wallet.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays rent + signs the tx. Their key is NOT stored on the message; note
the fee-payer is still observable in the transaction itself.

instructions.name: set_circle_config
docs: Set a Circle's tunable policy (donation-on-renew, member-vote
quorum/pass thresholds, treasury allowlist). Any seat; PDA ["config", circle].

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (signs + pays the config rent on first set).

instructions.name: set_circle_country
docs: Set a Circle's country (ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. "FR") for the
foundation directory's continent → country grouping. Any Council seat may
set it; a separate PDA, so existing Circles need no migration.
PDA: ["country", circle].

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (signs + pays the marker rent on first set).

instructions.name: set_faucet_amount
docs: Treasurer tunes the per-grant amount, within the absolute on-chain cap.

accounts.name: treasurer
docs: The Treasurer seat (seat 0).

instructions.name: set_meetings
docs: Publish/replace a Circle's meeting calendar (recurring + sessions JSON).

instructions.name: set_membership_mint
docs: Register the Circle's Token-2022 NonTransferable (soulbound) membership mint.

accounts.name: treasurer
docs: Must be the Council's Treasurer seat.

instructions.name: set_open_membership
docs: Set the Circle's membership-admission policy: `open = true` makes joining
permissionless (anyone self-admits); `open = false` restores Scribe-Secretary
validation. Any Council seat may toggle it. Uses a separate marker PDA, so
the `Circle` account (and every existing Circle) is untouched.

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (signs + pays the marker rent on first toggle).

instructions.name: set_personhood
docs: Configure the Circle's sybil gate (on/off + the unique-human Merkle root).

accounts.name: secretary
docs: Must be the Council's Secretary seat.

instructions.name: set_recovery
docs: Member configures their own recovery: set/rotate the guardian key and the
require-co-sign policy (signed by owner or current recovery key).

accounts.name: member_authority
docs: The member's current `owner` or a guardian `recovery_key`.

instructions.name: set_treasury_allow
docs: Add/remove a treasury withdrawal recipient on a Circle's spend allowlist
(any seat). Enforced by `withdraw_treasury` when the allowlist is on.

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (signs + pays the marker rent on first set).

instructions.name: set_treasury_wallet
docs: Write the Circle's treasury steward wallet, authorized by an executed
4-of-7 `SetTreasuryWallet` proposal.

accounts.name: multisig
docs: the exact pubkey the Council voted for AND an initialized SPL Token / Token-2022
multisig (m ≥ 2). Not deserialized as a typed account so either token program's
multisig is accepted.

instructions.name: set_two_sponsor_admission
docs: Any Council seat toggles the two-sponsor admission policy: parrain (any
member in good standing) + trusted servant (any of the 7 seats).

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (signs + pays the marker's rent on first use).

instructions.name: set_visibility
docs: A member sets their per-element visibility (Epic 5): avatar/quipu/bio each
to tier 0 (chosen) / 1 (my circle) / 2 (all members). Default is my circle.

accounts.name: member
docs: A key the member controls (owner or guardian); signs + pays rent.

instructions.name: tie_quipu_cord
docs: The sponsor ties a quipu cord for a completed step (Epic 3): one cord per
(member, step), step 1..=12, colour derived off-chain from the step.

accounts.name: member_membership
docs: The walker's membership.

accounts.name: sponsor_membership
docs: The sponsor's membership (the wing side of the bond).

accounts.name: wing_peer
docs: The member's sponsor bond — seed-bound to the member, so it can't be
swapped for someone else's.

accounts.name: cord
docs: One cord per (member, step) — `init` collision IS the refusal of a second.

accounts.name: sponsor
docs: The sponsor (signs + pays the cord's rent — the closing act of the rite).

instructions.name: update_circle_location
docs: Update only a Circle's location (coordinates + city + address) on its
existing directory profile — name & doc CIDs untouched. Overwrite only,
no location history kept. Any Council seat may move the Circle.

accounts.name: profile
docs: The Circle's directory profile — must already exist (created via
`upsert_circle_profile`). `has_one = circle` ties it to this Circle.

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat may relocate the Circle.

instructions.name: upsert_circle_profile
docs: Create/update a Circle's public directory profile (geo + IPFS doc CIDs)
that powers "Find a Circle Near You". Any Council seat may set it.

accounts.name: seat
docs: Any Council seat (signs + pays).

instructions.name: verify_disclosure
docs: Verify an acknowledgment selective-disclosure proof against a gate's
predicate requirements and mint an AccessPass (predicate-gated access).

instructions.name: verify_fellow_member
docs: F56 — verify a visiting member of a sibling Circle against its anchored
root; mints an anonymous VisitPass.

accounts.name: home_circle
docs: The visitor's home Circle — in this federation (direct-parent rule).

accounts.name: host_circle
docs: The Circle being visited — also in this federation.

accounts.name: anchor_entry
docs: The home Circle's published root — seed-bound to (foundation, home), so
a proof can only be checked against the root genuinely anchored for
that Circle.

accounts.name: visit_pass
docs: One pass per member per host Circle (`init` collision = already
verified; the pass persists — no need to re-prove).

accounts.name: payer
docs: A relayer pays, so the visitor's wallet never appears.

instructions.name: withdraw_treasury
docs: Move treasury SOL, authorized by an executed 4-of-7 WithdrawTreasury proposal.

accounts.name: config
docs: The Circle's policy (its `treasury_allowlist` flag). Seed-bound +
created on first use, so it can't be omitted to dodge an enabled allowlist.

accounts.name: allow
docs: The recipient's allowlist entry — only required when the allowlist is on.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Whoever triggers the (still-permissionless) withdrawal; pays config rent
on first use. The transaction fee-payer anyway.

instructions.name: withdraw_treasury_token
docs: Move an SPL / Token-2022 treasury balance, authorized by an executed 4-of-7
`WithdrawTreasuryToken` proposal. Without this, `donate_token` deposits were
unrecoverable (no treasury-PDA signing path for tokens).

accounts.name: config
docs: The Circle's policy (its `treasury_allowlist` flag). Seed-bound + created
on first use, so it can't be omitted to dodge an enabled allowlist.

accounts.name: allow
docs: The recipient wallet's allowlist entry — only required when the allowlist
is on.

accounts.name: mint
docs: Must equal the proposal's pinned mint.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: The treasury PDA — signs the transfer.

accounts.name: treasury_token_account
docs: The treasury's token account for `mint`, owned by the treasury PDA.

accounts.name: recipient
docs: account's authority is checked against this below).

accounts.name: recipient_token_account
docs: The recipient's token account for `mint`.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Whoever triggers the (still-permissionless) withdrawal; pays config rent on
first use.

errors.name: NameTooLong
errors.msg: Circle name exceeds maximum length

errors.name: MembershipExpired
errors.msg: Membership has expired

errors.name: Unauthorized
errors.msg: Caller is not the circle authority

errors.name: InvalidLineageProof
errors.msg: Invalid lineage / level-grant proof

errors.name: NonIncreasingLevel

errors.name: PoseidonError

errors.name: LineageFull

errors.name: AlreadyFinalized

errors.name: MintInitFailed

errors.name: FaucetCapExceeded

errors.msg: Faucet jar has insufficient funds for the grant

errors.name: NotParrain
errors.msg: Signer is not the neophyte's designated parrain (WingPeer)

errors.name: NeophyteWalletUnset

errors.name: FaucetAmountCooling
errors.msg: Faucet grant amount changed recently; grants resume after the cooldown

errors.name: FaucetRefillTooLarge
errors.msg: Faucet refill exceeds the maximum a single vote may move

errors.name: TwoSponsorRequired
errors.msg: This Circle admits by two-sponsor attestation — use the provisional admission flow

errors.name: TwoSponsorNotEnabled
errors.msg: Two-sponsor admission is not enabled for this Circle

errors.name: SelfAttestation
errors.msg: A member cannot attest for their own admission

errors.name: ParrainCannotConfirm
errors.msg: The trusted servant must be a different person than the parrain

errors.name: InvalidStep
errors.msg: Quipu step must be between 1 and 12

errors.name: InvalidVisibilityTier
errors.msg: Visibility tier must be 0 (chosen), 1 (my circle), or 2 (all members)

errors.name: RootNotRecent
errors.msg: Proof root is not the current member root nor a recent one

errors.name: AnchorMismatch
errors.msg: Proof root does not match the published anchor root for that Circle

errors.name: NotInGoodStanding
errors.msg: Membership is not live (expired or still provisional)

types.name: AccessPass
docs: A durable proof-of-eligibility minted by `verify_disclosure`: it records that
some acknowledgment satisfied a gate's predicate requirements. A downstream
program (a ceremony, a resource) checks the pass exists for its `gate`.

fields.name: requirements_hash
docs: keccak(DisclosureGate) — the exact predicate policy this pass was minted
under. A consumer MUST check this equals the hash of its own required
policy, so a pass minted under weaker requirements can't be reused.

types.name: Acknowledgment
docs: An acknowledgment credential — a course/initiation certificate attesting
"portrait PPP followed course CCC, taught by XXX, on date DDD". Only the
Poseidon root `root = Poseidon(cP, cC, cX, cD)` of the four blinded field
commitments is stored, so nothing about the fields is public. The holder
later opens any subset with a ZK proof (`circuits/ack_disclose.circom`).
`issuer_attested` is set true because issuance verified an *issuer-anonymous*
lineage proof: a teacher of level >= `attest_level` in the lineage tree
authorized this `root` — so "taught by a real lineage holder" is guaranteed
without recording which teacher. See docs/acknowledgments.md.

types.name: AdmissionAttestation
docs: The parrain's attestation for one newcomer (Epic 1, attestation A). One per
newcomer — the PDA seed is the refusal of a second. Two forms:
* **Named (pilot)** — `attest_admission`: `parrain` records the attesting
membership's commitment (needed for the distinct-persons rule; no more
linkable than the WingPeer bond the pilot already accepts), `nullifier`
is zero.
* **Anonymous (Epic 2)** — `attest_admission_zk`: `parrain` is zero and
`nullifier = Poseidon(secret, newcomer)` from a Groth16 proof that SOME
member of the tree attested — the sponsor edge never exists on-chain.
PDA: ["attest", circle, newcomer_commitment] — one parrain either way.

fields.name: leaf_index
docs: Set by `confirm_admission`: 1 + the MemberTree leaf index the newcomer
was inserted at (1-BASED; 0 = not yet confirmed), and the member epoch
it belongs to (F54). Lets clients reconstruct the exact insertion order
even when confirmations interleave with direct issuance. Valid only
while `leaf_epoch` equals the Circle's current epoch
(`RecentRoots.epoch`); stale after an epoch rebuild (the reinsertion's
`EpochLeaf` supersedes it).

types.name: ChildCloseVote
docs: A foundation-led 4-of-7 vote to DELETE (close) a federation Circle, valid
for a chosen window. PDA: ["childclose", child, &nonce.to_le_bytes()].

types.name: ChildSeatVote
docs: A foundation-led vote to rotate a CHILD Circle's Council seats. The World
Service / foundation Circle (the child's `parent`) may help a member Circle
rotate its 7 seats: a 4-of-7 vote among the FOUNDATION's seats, valid for a
chosen window (1–90 days), that — once it reaches threshold before expiry —
writes the new seat set into the child's Council via `execute_child_rotation`.
This is the one cross-Circle authority: the parent can rotate a direct
child's seats. PDA: ["childvote", child, &nonce.to_le_bytes()].

types.name: Circle
docs: A Circle — a local AHA group, forked under the World Service Circle.
Governance (proposals/voting) lives in a Realms Realm; the treasury in a
Squads multisig. This account holds the membership/Council/lineage state that
those tools do not provide.

fields.name: parent
docs: The parent Circle this one is nested under (the World Service Circle's
address, or a fixed root for the foundation itself). A PDA seed + the
federation link — never an actor. There is NO admin key: the **Council is
the authority** (group conscience), so a Circle is governed only by its
7 seats.

fields.name: council
docs: The 7-seat Council (3 named servants + 4 elders) — the Circle's authority;
threshold 4-of-7.

fields.name: membership_period
docs: Length of one membership term, in seconds (e.g. one year).

fields.name: require_personhood
docs: Sybil gate: if true, `issue_membership` requires a `PersonhoodCredential`
(one human → one membership per Circle) proven against `personhood_root`.

fields.name: personhood_root
docs: Merkle root of a unique-human set (e.g. a World ID group, or a Circle's
vouching set) that personhood proofs are checked against.

fields.name: membership_mint
docs: Token-2022 NonTransferable (soulbound) membership mint, if configured.
`default()` = none. Mint authority must be this Circle PDA.

fields.name: name
docs: Human-readable Circle name (also a PDA seed, so <= MAX_NAME bytes).

types.name: CircleConfig
docs: Per-Circle tunable policy — a sibling PDA so the `Circle` layout is untouched
and existing Circles need no migration. Any Council seat sets it; it is
created on first use with safe defaults (no donation, classic ⅓-quorum +
simple-majority voting, treasury allowlist off). PDA: ["config", circle].
The full layout is defined up front so the donation / quorum / allowlist
features can be wired in incrementally without ever re-migrating the account.

fields.name: renew_donation_lamports
docs: Donation (lamports) required *into the treasury* to renew a membership
(Tradition 7 — self-support). 0 = renewal is free.

fields.name: vote_quorum_num
docs: Member-vote quorum as num/den of the eligible set (0 den ⇒ default ⅓).

fields.name: vote_pass_num
docs: Member-vote pass threshold as yes/turnout (0 den ⇒ default simple majority).

fields.name: treasury_allowlist
docs: When true, a treasury withdrawal recipient must hold a TreasuryAllow marker.

types.name: CircleCountry
docs: A Circle's country — an ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. "FR"), set by any
Council seat. Powers the foundation directory's continent → country grouping
(the continent is derived client-side from the code). A separate PDA, so the
`Circle`/`CircleProfile` layouts are untouched and existing Circles need no
migration. PDA: ["country", circle].

types.name: CircleMeetings
docs: A Circle's meeting calendar — recurring patterns + exceptional sessions —
as a compact JSON string every member (and visitor) can read. Set by any
Council seat. Separate PDA so the `Circle`/`CircleProfile` layouts are
untouched. PDA: ["meetings", circle].

types.name: CircleProfile
docs: Public directory profile for a Circle — powers the "Find a Circle Near You"
map and the shared-document links. Optional and separate from `Circle` (so it
never touches the audited core account); a Circle with no profile simply
doesn't appear on the map. Set/updated by any Council seat via
`upsert_circle_profile`. Coordinates are fixed-point **microdegrees**
(degrees × 1e6) to avoid floats: lat ∈ [-90e6, 90e6], lon ∈ [-180e6, 180e6].
The IPFS CIDs point to the Circle's shared material (12 Steps, Preamble, and
the Daily Reflections collection), fetched read-only from a public gateway.

types.name: CircleRootAnchor
docs: F56 — fellowship-wide verification anchor: a Circle's member root published
under its foundation, so any Circle in the same federation can verify a
visiting member's proof without holding the visitor's home tree. Written by
the permissionless `publish_member_root` crank (it only copies verified
on-chain state); parentage is constraint-checked with the same rule the
federation-governance fixes hardened (`child.parent == foundation`).
PDA: ["anchor", foundation, circle].

fields.name: recovery_timelock
docs: Seconds a `MigrateWallet` must wait after reaching threshold before it
can execute — the contest window during which any seat may cancel it.

types.name: DisclosureGate
docs: What a gate demands of a disclosure before granting access.

fields.name: expected_date_lower_bound
docs: The date the proof's `dateOk` boolean must have been evaluated against.
`dateLowerBound` is a prover-supplied public input, so without pinning it
the prover could set it to 0 and satisfy any "completed after X" gate. The
gate must therefore declare the exact threshold it requires.

fields.name: expected_catalog_root
docs: Trusted, pinned roots the proof's predicate must have been checked against
(a prover could otherwise pass a self-made set root).

types.name: EpochLeaf
docs: F54b — one re-inserted leaf of an epoch rebuild. PDA
["epochleaf", circle, epoch_le, commitment]; `init` collision is the
double-reinsertion guard. `leaf_index` lets clients reconstruct the new
tree's insertion order exactly.

types.name: FaucetJar
docs: A Circle's gas faucet — first-transaction-fee mutual aid for newly admitted
members (Trust Platform Epic 0, Tradition 7). The jar's lamports live ON this
account; anyone may top it up by plain transfer, but treasury→jar refills
require a passed anonymous member vote (`refill_faucet`), and outflows happen
only through `activate_faucet` — one uniform grant per neophyte, ever,
triggered by the neophyte's designated parrain (their WingPeer).
`grant_lamports` is Treasurer-tunable but the program itself enforces the
absolute cap `FAUCET_MAX_GRANT_LAMPORTS` — the cap is revised at the equinox
by governance (a program upgrade), never by a price oracle.
Every grant pays exactly `grant_lamports`, and uniformity is enforced rather
than merely intended: a retune stamps `amount_changed_at`, and no grant may
be paid until `FAUCET_AMOUNT_COOLDOWN` has elapsed. Without that wait a
Treasurer could set a distinctive amount immediately before one neophyte's
activation and restore it after, tagging that person's wallet with a
correlatable transfer — exactly the fingerprint uniform amounts exist to
prevent. PDA: ["faucet", circle].

fields.name: grant_lamports
docs: Lamports paid out per grant (Treasurer-set, ≤ FAUCET_MAX_GRANT_LAMPORTS).

fields.name: granted
docs: Jar-level accounting: how many grants this jar has ever paid. Jar-level,
never member-level — nothing here counts or ranks a person.

fields.name: amount_changed_at
docs: Unix time `grant_lamports` was last changed (0 = never). Grants wait out
`FAUCET_AMOUNT_COOLDOWN` after a change, so an amount can never be aimed
at an individual.

types.name: FederationChild
docs: F56 — a foundation's CONSENT that `circle` is genuinely part of its
federation. Without this, `circle.parent == foundation` proves nothing:
`initialize_circle` is permissionless and `parent` is caller-set, so an
attacker could self-claim a real foundation as parent, anchor an
attacker-controlled root, and forge a fellow-member `VisitPass` at every
host in the federation (ultracode CRITICAL, 2026-08-11b). This PDA — created
only by a **foundation Council seat** via `approve_federation_child` — is the
missing consent: `publish_member_root` requires it, so only foundation-vetted
children can be anchored, and `verify_fellow_member` (which needs the anchor)
is transitively gated. `state.rs`'s own note that `parent` is "a link, never
an actor" is why the actor must be this explicit approval. PDA:
["fedchild", foundation, circle].

types.name: LevelGrant
docs: Record of a single shamanic level grant along an anonymous lineage.
`issuer_commitment` is the ZK commitment of the granting shaman — recorded
so the chain of transmission can be re-proved later, WITHOUT revealing the
granter's identity on-chain.

types.name: Lineage
docs: The append-only Poseidon Merkle tree of lineage credentials for a Circle.
`root` is what ZK `grant_level` proofs are checked against. Incremental
insertion state (`filled_subtrees`, `next_index`) follows the Tornado
MerkleTreeWithHistory pattern. See docs/zk-lineage.md.

types.name: MaciMessage
docs: One encrypted MACI command (vote or key-change), sealed to the round's
coordinator with a single-use ephemeral key. Append-only; the coordinator
applies last-valid-per-voter off-chain, so a later message overrides an
earlier (coerced) one. PDA: ["macimsg", round, index].

types.name: MaciRound
docs: A MACI (Minimal Anti-Collusion Infrastructure) voting round bound to a member
proposal. Voters publish ENCRYPTED commands — a vote, or a key-change that
silently invalidates a coerced vote — sealed to the `coordinator` key, so no
observer or briber can see how anyone voted on-chain (receipt-freeness). The
coordinator decrypts the queue off-chain and submits a tally with a ZK proof
that it processed honestly; `tally_hash` records the verified result. This
account is the on-chain message queue + round state. PDA: ["maci", proposal].
(The process/tally circuits + coordinator service are specified in docs/maci.md.)

types.name: MemberProposal
docs: A group-conscience proposal voted on by the whole membership: an idea, or a
change to shared material/documentation. One member = one vote, cast
anonymously (Merkle inclusion in the snapshotted member set + a per-proposal
nullifier). `description_hash` commits to the off-chain text (e.g. an IPFS CID
hash). See docs/member-voting.md.

types.name: MemberTree
docs: The append-only Poseidon Merkle tree of *member* identity commitments for a
Circle (the votable population). Same shape as `Lineage`; `next_index` is the
member count. A commitment is inserted at `issue_membership`. Member voting
proves Semaphore-style inclusion against a snapshot of `root`.

types.name: Membership
docs: A yearly, non-transferable (soulbound) membership.
For anonymity the member is identified by a ZK `commitment` (a Poseidon/
keccak hash of their secret identity), NOT by a wallet — so on-chain reads
never reveal who the member is. A Token-2022 NonTransferable token may be
minted alongside for selective public disclosure.

fields.name: level
docs: Highest shamanic level attained (0 = none).

fields.name: owner
docs: Optional controlling wallet for selective disclosure. `default()` means
fully anonymous (no wallet bound). This is the field a 4-of-7 wallet
migration rebinds during key recovery.

fields.name: recovery_keys
docs: Up to two optional guardian/backup keys the member controls separately
from `owner` (1-of-2: either can act, so losing one guardian still leaves
recovery possible). Lets a member self-migrate or co-sign even after
losing the owner key, and preserves anonymity (owner may stay `default()`
while a guardian is set). Unused slots are `default()`.

fields.name: require_cosign
docs: If true, a Council `MigrateWallet` cannot rebind this membership without a
signature from `owner` or a guardian — collusion-proof, but the
membership is unrecoverable if every key is lost.

types.name: Message
docs: An end-to-end encrypted 1:1 message with a SEALED SENDER: neither the program
nor the public chain stores who sent it. `eph_pubkey` is a fresh, single-use
x25519 key — it leaks no identity and gives the sender forward secrecy (its
secret half is destroyed right after send). The real sender is named AND
signed *inside* the ciphertext, and the recipient verifies that signature
after decrypting. The ciphertext is always exactly `CT_LEN` bytes (the
plaintext is padded before sealing), so every message looks identical
on-chain — no message-length leak. `expires_at` (0 = never) lets clients hide
it and anyone close it afterwards. PDA: ["msg", recipient, &id.to_le_bytes()].
NOTE (documented limitation): the *recipient* and *timing* are unavoidably
public (the recipient finds their mail by querying their own address), and
the transaction fee-payer still links a message to whoever paid for it. True
sender anonymity would need a relayer/mixnet — out of scope here.

types.name: MessagingKey
docs: A wallet's published x25519 messaging public key (signature-derived), so
others can encrypt private messages to it. PDA: ["msgkey", owner].

types.name: Nullifier
docs: A spent ZK nullifier. Existence == "this grant has already been made";
Anchor `init` fails if the PDA already exists, giving replay protection.

types.name: OpenMembership
docs: Per-Circle membership-admission policy, kept in its own PDA so the `Circle`
layout is untouched and every existing Circle keeps deserializing.
Absent (the default for every Circle) ⇒ the **Scribe-Secretary** seat admits
members — validation required. Present with `open == true` ⇒ **permissionless**:
anyone may self-admit a membership. Toggled by any Council seat via
`set_open_membership`; consulted (optionally) by `issue_membership`.
PDA: ["openjoin", circle].

types.name: PersonhoodCredential
docs: Proof that a unique human is eligible for one membership in a Circle, minted
by `prove_personhood` after an anonymous proof-of-personhood (World ID-style).
Its PDA is seeded by the personhood nullifier, so one human yields exactly one
credential per Circle; `issue_membership` consumes it (`used = true`) — one
human, one membership. The human's identity is never revealed.

types.name: Post
docs: A member-authored post / bulletin for a Circle (F30). Text and/or an IPFS
image, shown only within [start_date, end_date]. Authored by a member (a
wallet that owns a live membership in the Circle); deletable by ANY of the 7
Council seats at any time. PDA: ["post", circle, author, &nonce.to_le_bytes()].

types.name: ProgressToken
docs: A progress token — an on-chain milestone "chip" celebrating a member's
journey (e.g. 30 / 90 / 365 days), attested by a Council seat. One per
(member, milestone). PDA: ["progress", circle, member, milestone].

types.name: Proposal
docs: A pending Council decision. Approvals are a bitmask over the 7 seats, so a
seat can approve only once and a tally is `count_ones()`.

fields.name: drained
docs: For `WithdrawTreasury`: set true once the lamports have actually moved, so
an executed proposal cannot be replayed to drain the treasury repeatedly.

fields.name: eligible_at
docs: Earliest unix time the proposal may execute; 0 = not yet armed (threshold
unmet). Set when approvals first reach threshold: `now` for RotateSeat,
`now + recovery_timelock` for MigrateWallet.

types.name: ProposalAction
docs: What a 4-of-7 vote authorizes.

types.name: ProvisionalMember
docs: Marks a membership as provisional (Epic 1 / Epic 9): admitted on the
parrain's attestation alone, awaiting the trusted servant's co-attestation.
While this marker exists the commitment is NOT in the MemberTree, so every
members-only proof (votes, elections) fails by construction — the one-way
glass is structural, not cosmetic. The faucet still works: `activate_faucet`
checks the membership account, not the tree. `confirm_admission` inserts the
commitment into the tree and closes this marker.
PDA: ["provisional", circle, commitment].

types.name: QuipuCord
docs: One quipu cord — a single step of the twelve, completed and tied by the
member's sponsor as the closing act of the ceremony (Trust Platform Epic 3).
Binary and personal by design: the account either exists (you walked the
step) or it does not. There is NO score, no fraction, no "N of 12" — the
only fields are which step and when. The cord's alchemical COLOUR is not
stored on-chain; it is derived from `step` client-side (see
`frontend/lib/quipu.ts` and `docs/quipu.md`), so the colour mapping can be
finalised against the Emerald correspondence table without a chain change.
`sponsor` is the tying sponsor's membership commitment (the wing bond), so
the ceremony's closing act is recorded as anonymously as the memberships
themselves. One cord per (member, step). PDA: ["quipu", circle, member, step].

types.name: RecentRoots
docs: F54a — ring buffer of a Circle's recent MemberTree roots, plus the current
member epoch (F54b). Companion PDA ["roots", circle] so the already-deployed
MemberTree layout never changes. Written by the permissionless `note_root`
crank (run by a prover right before proving, so the root they prove against
survives concurrent insertions) and by `begin_member_epoch`/`reinsert_member`.
A proof verified against ANY root in the buffer is accepted where the
instruction opts in (attest_admission_zk) — a bounded staleness window, not
an unbounded one: the buffer holds `N` roots and old ones are overwritten.

fields.name: epoch
docs: Member epoch — 0 until the first `begin_member_epoch` rebuild. Each
rebuild increments it and empties the tree; only live memberships are
re-inserted, which is what makes the votable set a GOOD-STANDING set.

fields.name: epoch_started_at
docs: When the current epoch began (0 for epoch 0).

fields.name: index
docs: Next write position in `roots` (wraps at N).

fields.name: roots
docs: Last N roots, zero entries = never written.

types.name: SeatElection
docs: Binds a member proposal (F6 anonymous ZK ballot) to a seat election: if the
proposal passes, `candidate` is installed into `council.seats[seat_index]`
(group-conscience election of a servant). The proposal's `description_hash`
MUST equal H("AHA-elect" || seat_index || candidate), so the machine-readable
outcome is exactly what members anonymously voted on. PDA: ["election", proposal].

types.name: TreasuryAllow
docs: Treasury allowlist entry: marks `recipient` as permitted to receive a
withdrawal from `circle` (only enforced when `CircleConfig.treasury_allowlist`
is on). PDA: ["treasallow", circle, recipient].

types.name: TreasuryConfig
docs: The Circle's designated treasury steward wallet (governed by a 4-of-7
`SetTreasuryWallet` vote, applied by `set_treasury_wallet`). Separate PDA so
the `Circle` layout is untouched. Absent ⇒ none set (the treasury PDA itself
remains the only custodian). PDA: ["treasurycfg", circle].

types.name: TwoSponsorAdmission
docs: Per-Circle two-sponsor admission policy (Trust Platform Epic 1, amended
v0.2). Absent or `required == false` ⇒ admission works as before (F4
Secretary-gated, or F31 open). Present with `required == true` ⇒ every
admission needs the asymmetric attestation pair: the **parrain** (any member
in good standing) and a **trusted servant** (any of the 7 Council seats),
two different people. Sibling PDA so the `Circle` layout is untouched.
PDA: ["twosponsor", circle].

types.name: VisibilityPolicy
docs: A member's per-element visibility policy (Trust Platform Epic 5): who may see
each element of their page — the avatar, the quipu, the bio — chosen
independently. The audience widens through three tiers:
0 = ChosenOnes   (only members the owner has chosen)
1 = MyCircle     (members of this Circle) — the DEFAULT for every element
2 = AllMembers   (any member of the fellowship — the widest audience that
exists; nothing is ever visible to the public internet)
Absent ⇒ every element defaults to `MyCircle` (tier 1): the protective
default gives disclosure its social meaning, and opening up is a deliberate
act. A viewer outside an element's audience sees the element simply absent —
there is NO "hidden" indicator, so a sparse newcomer's page and a private
elder's page look identical. PDA: ["visibility", circle, member].
This is the policy engine. Cryptographic enforcement of `MyCircle` (a ZK
circle-membership proof on the read path, inheriting Epic 2's machinery) and
the encrypted per-tier key distribution for avatar/bio are the remaining
Phase-2 work; the quipu is on-chain and gated by this policy directly.

types.name: VisitPass
docs: F56 — proof that AN anonymous member of `home_circle` verified themselves to
`host_circle`. The nullifier is Poseidon(secret, host_circle_field) — one
pass per member per host Circle, deterministic, naming no one. PDA:
["visit", host_circle, nullifier].

types.name: WingPeer
docs: A WingPeer relationship — a more-experienced member ("wing") who takes a
newer member ("mentee") under their wing (the fellowship's sponsor bond).
Both are memberships of the same Circle, identified by commitment so the
pairing stays as anonymous as the memberships. One primary wing per mentee.
PDA: ["wingpeer", circle, mentee].
